integration.r4_fix: RED triage of the first clean full-scale run (run_20260801_133914: user cleaned all run_* dirs first, still 8782 files / 21 RED / 483 Hydra) proved the remaining findings were canonical, in three classes. (1) 16 VRN registry JSONs fail strict parsing only because string values contain raw control characters - R4 adds a deterministic sandbox repair (lenient strict=False parse, strict re-serialize, round-trip verify; repair_type JSON_CONTROL_CHARACTER_ESCAPE, candidate-only). (2) supportive modules/ui_support/iconforge_console_data.json is 1.99 GB and json.loads dies with MemoryError - R4 adds a 64 MiB content-analysis guard: oversized files stay inventoried/hashed but content parsing is skipped (metrics.content_analysis=SKIPPED_LARGE_FILE). (3) 317 RED Hydra risks were vendored files under functional modules/VDF/_vdf_envs/*/Lib/site-packages plus a full snapshot tree under VAP/ASSETS/SCOPE_COPY - R4 excludes _vdf_envs, site-packages and scope_copy like venv/received_duplicates. Remaining genuine defect: 4 byte-identical, syntactically broken copies of Invoke-VIA-VRN-OneClick-Sidebar-v0159.ps1 (v0161D/v0162/v0162A/v0162B child dirs) - real breakage, operator decision (archive or repair), not auto-fixable. Verified live on a seeded base reproducing all classes: control-char JSON pre-RED then post-GREEN via sandbox candidate, oversized file GREEN-skipped (both threshold sides unit-tested), exclusions leave zero rows and zero Hydra, only the broken ps1 stays RED. Both daily entrypoints re-locked to the R4 launcher SHA.
integration.r3_fix: First full-scale Windows panoramic run (2026-08-01, 8782 files) ended ROUND_REVIEW_REQUIRED_RED_ERRORS_REMAIN with the RED count oscillating 20-21 across rounds and 483 Hydra / 1640 SSOT groups. Root cause: the inventory walked the engine's own runtime root (supportive modules/.../v0162B/runtime), re-analyzing prior runs' sandbox copies, evidence files and the truncated corpses left by the earlier [Errno 28] disk-full crash - RED errors no sandbox repair can converge, plus duplicate-basename Hydra/SSOT noise. R3 excludes the engine's own runtime root (run_dir parent) from inventory. Companion: qa/via_red_triage_v001.py + VIA.ps1 -Do Report distill any run (including pre-R3 runs) into a paste-sized RED triage Markdown. Verified live: a base seeded with a corrupt old run_* directory (invalid JSON + Python syntax error + duplicate engine basename) gates UNIFIED_SANDBOX_GREEN with zero runtime-polluted inventory rows. Both daily entrypoints re-locked to the R3 launcher SHA.

integration.r2_fix: First Windows runtime user test (2026-07-28 15:34, py 3.13.7) exposed an argument-quoting defect: Start-Process joined array arguments without quoting, so the engine path containing spaces ('supportive modules') was split and Python failed with Errno 2. R2 quotes every whitespace-containing argument explicitly and passes one command line. Both daily entrypoints re-locked to the R2 launcher SHA.

integration.r5_fix: The operator user-test run that closed R4 (run of 2026-08-02 09:14: 7468 files / 0 RED / 0 YELLOW) left 317 Hydra rows, every one a DUPLICATE_BASENAME_DIFFERENT_HASH whose extra copies live in timestamped snapshot trees (RUN_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS report archives, e.g. _via_safe_polyglot_optimizer RUN_* reports) or the VAP source-import staging area (SOURCE_VAP_MODULE version folders 1-13 and html_template). Those trees exist to preserve history, so differing hashes there are provenance, not runtime divergence. R5 scores Hydra risk only on copies outside archive scope; collisions confined to archive scope are kept visible as GREEN ARCHIVE_SNAPSHOT_DUPLICATE rows, and the overall gate plus the HYDRA summary count consider only non-GREEN rows. Detection itself (A03) stays fully enabled: two or more divergent copies outside archive scope still raise YELLOW/RED exactly as before.
